title: Predictor information content vs. algorithm choice in ML estimation of daily solar energy: code, data and results (10 Brazilian cities, NASA/POWER 2020-2025)
description:
Code, input data and results accompanying the manuscript Predictor Information Content Versus Algorithm Choice in Machine Learning Estimation of Daily Solar Energy: A Temporally Validated Benchmark for Ten Brazilian Cities (F. de L. Caneppele et al., submitted to IEEE Access, 2026).

Six regression models (linear, CART, SVR, random forest, gradient boosted trees, additive spline) and three nested predictor sets (meteorological; + astronomical; + satellite cloud amount) are evaluated for daily all-sky solar energy at ten Brazilian state capitals using NASA/POWER daily data. Training, tuning and model selection use 2020-2023 only; 2024 and 2025 are independent test years. Results are reported as skill against climatology and persistence with Diebold-Mariano tests (HAC variance, Holm correction), grouped permutation importance and covariate-shift diagnostics.

Funding: CNPq (Brazil), Grant 401718/2023-9. NASA/POWER data: NASA Langley Research Center POWER Project.
